subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@avatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up

Hi Sara — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: power AvaTech search suggestions and realtime personalization with an LLM-backed scoring model.
- Target SLAs: 95th percentile latency <= 100ms for 1-2k RPS sustained during business hours; peaks up to 4k RPS.
- Average tokens per request ~ 120 (prompt+context); longest flows up to 300 tokens.
- Data constraints: no sensitive PII in prompts, but IP-protected model outputs — Avatech would prefer data isolation if feasible.

Questions for your team so we can recommend mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):
1) Do you have a current traffic profile (RPS by hour) or a PRD we can use?
2) Are you expecting steady 24/7 traffic or primarily daytime peaks?
3) Any procurement constraints around reserved capacity / committed spend?

Recommendation approach: run a 2-week pilot on our hosted API to validate latency/throughput and caching profiles. If you need guaranteed reserved throughput and strict isolation, we can scope Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) next — we can provide an apples-to-apples perf run.

Attaching the short requirements worksheet you can fill out (AVA_prod_requirements.xlsx) — if you send the traffic profile I can schedule perf tests with our infra team.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Mobile: +1 415-555-0182

--
Attachment: AVA_prod_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@avatech.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up

Thanks Neha — great recap. Quick answers below and a couple follow-ups.

- Traffic: weekdays 9am-6pm PST are busiest. Baseline ~1.5k RPS, peaks ~3.8k for short bursts (5-10m).
- Tokens: confirmed ~120 avg, 280 max for longer context.
- Procurement: we prefer not to commit to long annual reserved spend without an initial verification run. Procurement ok with a 30-day pilot PO.

Question: if we stay on Hosted for the pilot, can you achieve 95p <= 100ms at 1.5k RPS? If not, what would Dedicated latency look like for the same config?

Also looping in Tom (ops) to help with the traffic export.

Sara Jones
Product Lead, Search — Avatech
sara.jones@avatech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up

Neha — quick internal note after Sara's reply. Short summary and suggested position to recommend to the customer: 

- Given avg 120 tokens and target 95p <= 100ms at 1.5k RPS, hosted API can likely hit those numbers in a pilot if we enable aggressive prefix caching and continuous batching optimizations; however sustained multi-thousand RPS with tight p95 under 100ms points toward Dedicated for predictable latency and isolation.
- Dedicated gives guaranteed GPU pool, more predictable kernel choices and room for quantized model variants if they want to optimize cost later.
- Procurement preference for pilot without a big commitment — suggest proposing a 14-30 day hosted pilot with defined perf SLAs and a clear mutual action plan to transition to Dedicated if p95 targets are not met at target RPS.

I'll draft a recommended reply that balances risk — propose host pilot + opt-in path to Dedicated. If you want me to include estimated pricing delta for dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted baseline, I can pull numbers.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

> On Thu, Jun 4, 2026 at 9:12 AM Sara Jones wrote:
> > Quick answers below and a couple follow-ups.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@avatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up

Hi Sara — thanks for the data. Based on your traffic profile and procurement preference, here's a recommended path forward and next steps: 

1) Pilot on Hosted API (2 weeks) — what we propose:
   - Objective: validate 95p latency <= 100ms at baseline 1.5k RPS and observe peak behavior up to ~4k RPS.
   - Config: standard Redwood hosted model variant with prefix/KV caching enabled, continuous batching tuned for your token mix, and a dedicated testing window we coordinate with your ops team.
   - Success criteria: 95p <= 100ms for baseline window; clear degradation map for bursts. If criteria met, continue on hosted with ops monitoring.

2) Escalation path to Dedicated:
   - If pilot fails to meet latency SLOs due to sustained load or isolation needs, we'll provision Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with capacity sizing based on pilot telemetry (we typically size conservatively and iterate). Dedicated gives stronger p95 guarantees and lower variability under heavy load.

3) Procurement: we can accept a 30-day pilot PO for the Hosted pilot. If you prefer not to do Hosted, we can provide a fast quote for Dedicated but it will need a commitment window for reservation pricing.

Next steps:
- Can you share the traffic export from Tom? (HubSpot link updated here for mutual action plan: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/987654321)
- If you're good with the pilot approach I'll send the mutual action plan and pilot SOW (attached).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short alignment call this week if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
